task: Passive finite-state process learning and adaptive observable acquisition

claims.statement: For any passive-sample budget B and any estimator of the worst-history conditional transition probability, there are two stationary 2-state binary HMMs with common A-to-B transition epsilon, theta in {1/4,3/4}, deterministic full-rank emissions, full-rank transitions, and hidden-chain absolute spectral gap at least 1/4 such that max_theta E_theta[|theta_hat-theta|] >= (1-4 B epsilon)/4 when 4 B epsilon <= 1. The guarantee also covers arbitrary adaptive post-hoc observable selection from the same data.
assumptions: The learner receives at most B emitted symbols from one or more stationary reset episodes.
No intervention changes hidden transitions and no exact conditional-probability oracle is supplied.
The scored target is the conditional probability P(Y_{t+1}=1 | Y_t=1), under absolute loss.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary missing-context/coverage lower bound; no novelty or priority claim. It is narrower than an average-risk or fixed-horizon total-variation impossibility.
claims.costs: All observed output symbols, across all reset episodes, count toward B. Post-hoc computation is unrestricted. Active interventions or conditional oracles are outside the interface.
claims.falsifier: A proof audit finding a violated stationary-marginal union bound, an estimator whose output law on the all-zero transcript depends on theta beyond that transcript, or an arithmetic error in the triangle-inequality risk bound.
claims.next_gate: For a positive theorem, state an explicit lower bound on relevant context mass or provide a costed active policy guaranteeing visits; then compare worst-history and stationary-average losses separately.

claims.statement: The 2-state construction satisfies the rank assumptions in Hsu-Kakade-Zhang (positive stationary initial support and full-rank transition/emission matrices), while sigma_min(P_{2,1})=Theta(epsilon). The paper's finite-horizon spectral guarantee depends on inverse singular values of O and P_{2,1}; its separate conditional-KL guarantee is history-averaged and adds strict positivity assumptions that deterministic emissions violate.
assumptions: Hsu-Kakade-Zhang 2012 source statements are read at Condition 1, Theorem 6, Condition 3, and Theorem 7.
P_{2,1} uses rows for the second observation and columns for the first.
claims.novelty_boundary: A consistency/conditioning comparison, not a new spectral-learning theorem and not a refutation of Hsu-Kakade-Zhang.
claims.costs: Spectral learners use the same raw observation budget in the comparison. Their rank and singular-value promises must be charged as model conditions; the lower bound covers any estimator given those observations.
claims.falsifier: The source theorem has been misread, the pair-probability matrix formula or determinant is incorrect, or the claimed Theta(epsilon) singular-value scaling fails for either fixed theta value.
claims.next_gate: If benchmarking implementations, feed the same reset tuples and report both joint-law error and conditional error on the rare context; record numerical regularization and initialization.

claims.statement: Controlled partially observed system-identification results that assume chosen i.i.d. isotropic inputs, uniform stability under the input set, and persistence of excitation have a richer interface than passive HMM observations. Such active access may bypass the rare-context barrier only if its action costs and guaranteed state excitation are explicit.
assumptions: Comparison concerns Sattar-Jedra-Fazel-Dean 2025 bilinear-system model, not all system-identification methods.
Inputs and their stability/excitation promises are treated as supplied information, not free passive observations.
claims.novelty_boundary: No claim that this source solves passive HMM acquisition or guarantees rare hidden-state visits.
claims.costs: Input selection, actuation, reset, output sampling, and any history-feature dimension must be charged for an apples-to-apples comparison.
claims.falsifier: The cited paper's interface lacks the listed input/stability/excitation assumptions, or the proposed equal-information accounting incorrectly treats those actions as passive data.
claims.next_gate: Define a controlled finite-state process with an admissible action set and prove a quantitative visit/excitation guarantee under a charged policy.

claims.statement: Prior workspace analysis gives a stronger growing-state passive exact-acquisition lower bound: a fixed-rational irreducible and aperiodic binary m-state family has constant hidden spectral gap and an output distinction visited with probability at most 2^{-(m-1)} per time, implying Omega(2^m) passive symbols for exact identification; a larger-alphabet variant has full-rank emissions.
assumptions: The statement is inherited from the 7 October 2026 prior-workspace derivation and is not re-proved in this child report.
Exact model/output-series identification is the target; approximate fixed-horizon TV is excluded.
claims.novelty_boundary: No new result and no independent revalidation claimed in this task; cited only as a stronger existing artifact and comparison boundary.
claims.costs: Observed symbols across reset episodes count; arbitrary hidden-state control is excluded.
claims.falsifier: Review of the referenced inherited proof identifies a construction or coupling error.
claims.next_gate: Reopen and independently audit the exact m-state construction only if the parent synthesis relies on its full-rank or exponential-in-m strengthening.
